notes:
I couldn't write any notes on Jeremiah 36 this time, because none of the source pages came through.

I tried to load six pages: the Enduring Word chapter page, the Ellicott, Gill and Pulpit Commentary pages on BibleHub, the Precept Austin chapter page, and the NET Bible notes. My script crashed while it was handling a failed request. When I tried again, the tool told me I'd used up my searches and page loads for this turn. I didn't read any of the pages, so I have nothing from them to report.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, with a URL for every point, and never to fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written any verse notes. Anything I wrote now would come from memory, not from the sources, and it wouldn't be honest to attach URLs to it.

If you ask again in a new turn, I'll go through these pages and write the notes verse by verse:

- **Traditional reading:**
  - enduringword.com/bible-commentary/jeremiah-36/
  - biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/jeremiah/36.htm
  - biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/jeremiah/36.htm
  - biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/jeremiah/36.htm
  - preceptaustin.org
- **Where Protestant traditions differ:** searches on ligonier.org, thegospelcoalition.org, desiringgod.org, gty.org, wesley.nnu.edu (Wesley's Notes), lcms.org, 1517.org and spurgeon.org. Likely topics are the "perhaps" in verses 3 and 7 (God's foreknowledge and repentance), what the burned and rewritten scroll shows about Scripture lasting, and how verse 30 fits with Jehoiachin's short reign.
- **Other views:**
  - netbible.org notes and bibleodyssey.org, which may cover Baruch, the bullae (clay seal impressions) and how the book was put together
  - newadvent.org, catholic.com and oca.org, which may cover Baruch and how the Church reads Scripture
